name: wrocpp
description: Plugins that help Claude Code write C++ you would be happy to maintain, from the Wro.cpp community.

metadata.description: C++ plugins from Wro.cpp: C++26 reflection and idioms, quality gates, evidence-backed conventions, modules and fuzzing.

plugins.name: cpp26-guard
plugins.description: Keep C++26 code free of hand-written copies of definitions: reflection instead of enum-to-string switches, name tables, flag chains and key/member blocks, with concepts, import std, format and print and a comment policy. Skills, a pre-write advisory hook and tested lints with allowance files.

plugins.name: cpp-quality-gates
plugins.description: Make 'done' mean measured: a sanitizer matrix, a CRAP gate, mutation testing, coverage, compile-time undefined-behaviour checks and compiler capability tests, as skills with runnable scripts and CMake and CI templates.

plugins.name: cpp-conventions
plugins.description: Evidence-backed C++ conventions: designated initialisers, no needless copies, cppreference lookup, quantities as types and no magic numbers, each rule with compiler fixtures and an advisory pre-write scanner.

plugins.name: cpp-modules
plugins.description: Use import std and named modules with CMake and GCC 16: the experimental gate, a working template project and the traps that cost hours, each reproduced by a fixture.

plugins.name: cpp-fuzzing
plugins.description: Property-based and fuzz testing recipes for C++: one property function reused by AFL++ harnesses, corpus replay at compile time with #embed, bounded-exhaustive constexpr checks and compile-time undefined-behaviour detection.

plugins.name: tidy-agent
plugins.description: Run clang-tidy on every C++ file the agent edits, and turn recurring agent mistakes into tested clang-tidy checks. Pre-release; lives in wrocpp/tidy-agent.
